description:
src/methods/mod.rs public structs that are NOT marked `#[non_exhaustive]`:
- GetResponse<T> (line 29)
- QueryResponse (line 39)
- ChangesResponse (line 52)
- SetResponse<T> (line 69)
- SetError (line 84)
- QueryChangesResponse (line 102)
- AddedItem (line 114)
- CalendarEventParseResponse (line 132)
- PrincipalGetAvailabilityResponse (line 150)
- CalendarEventGetParams (line 165)
- SessionClient (line 232)

RFC 8620 §3.6, §5.1-§5.5, and the calendars draft all explicitly say servers MAY add response fields. Without `#[non_exhaustive]`, adding a new field to any of these is a SemVer-breaking change for callers who pattern-match exhaustively.

The recent commit history (`f9a3201 feat: non_exhaustive sweep`) shows this was intentional sweep work — it apparently didn't reach this crate. jmap-types and jmap-base-client are LOCKED with `#[non_exhaustive]` everywhere; this crate's public API is the gap.

Notably: `AddedItem` is exactly the kind of struct the spec is most likely to grow (recurrence-instance metadata, etc.).

Note: `CalendarEventGetParams` already has 3 fields and the spec adds new ones in subsequent draft versions — this struct WILL gain fields. Mark it now or pay later.
title: Public types missing #[non_exhaustive]
